newsitem.title: ITALY: Stefanel sees breakeven in 97, alliances.
newsitem.headline: Stefanel sees breakeven in 97, alliances.

text.p: Italian clothing group Stefanel still expects to break even this year and make money in 1998, confirming a strategy for commercial alliances that should result in distribution accords on foreign markets.
"We aim to break even in 1997, even if it will be a battle, and to return to profit in 1998," chairman Giuseppe Stefanel told reporters after the loss-making company's AGM.
"We are confident although cautious. We have positive signals from the market both in Italy and abroad," he added.
He said the group was currently in contact with potential new partners in certain important foreign markets but did not give any names.

"I can say that they are foreign partners, for commercial accords in a scenario of global reorganisation. These are distribution accords, very important for us on a strategic level and in the Far East," he added.

He said the first quarter of 1997 was "in line with the budget". As for longer term dividend prospects "there are all the indications that shareholders will be satisfied in 1998. But I think that boosting up the net assets of the company should come first in order of importance," he said.

Stefanel is going through a round of restructuring which it had initially hoped to bring it back to breakeven in 1996 from a net loss of 69.4 billion lire in 1995. But the group said in March it expected a loss of 16 billion lire for 1996 and pushed breakeven hopes out until 1997 and return to profit to 1998.
Stefanel shares slid earlier this month after it denied plans to sell out to the new powerful force in Italian textiles, the HPI -Marzotto grouping.
Queried on this, the chairman today again categorically denied there was any such operation underway.
At 1413 GMT, Stefanel was down 1.86 percent at 2,740 lire on a firmer Milan bourse. It had touched a high for this year of 3,300 lire on April 17, the day before it slumped on the company's denial.

"The speculative effect on the stock is not good," the chairman said. "We want the share price to grow in a healthy way, gradually, and fortunately it is holding up very well. We don't want it to rise to 5,000 lire only to fall to 3,000, we want it to go to 5,000 and stay there," he said.

Stefanel has already linked up with U.S. designer Calvin Klein in a joint venture to open a series of joint outlets selling the CK Calvin Klein line. But with the first outlet only opening in Milan last month, analysts said it will take some time for the ventures to make significant profits.
